data.description:
Verified each of the four cited urlquery.net reports directly:

2025-11-12 — thrill-data.com/waits/graph/quick/parkflow (theme park wait-time data). This is the earliest dated activity found anywhere in the corpus to date, roughly six months ahead of the May–September 2026 bulk of findings.
2025-11-28 — ittdashboard.nso.go.th/preview2en.php?id_project=118 (Thailand National Statistical Office). Confirmed failed: Cloudflare returned 525 (SSL handshake failed), matching the original note.
2026-03-06 — httpbin.org/base64/... relay fetching dataapi.oncb.go.th/suppress/case_per/2557 (Thailand Office of Narcotics Control Board, drug-suppression case statistics, Thai Buddhist year 2557 = 2014 CE). Plain public-data fetch and page-body dump; no attack payload in the decoded script.
2026-03-11 — httpbin.org/base64/... relay containing static pre-fetched text: Roi Et province labor-force statistics (Thai NSO dataset DF_02SUP, 2013–2021 by year). No live request in this one; the data is embedded directly in the base64 payload.

New, not in the original finding: urlquery's "related reports" for the NSO dashboard host show it was hit repeatedly well beyond the November 2025 failure — project IDs 95 and 102 recur multiple times between June 14 and June 19, 2026. This means interest in this specific Thai government statistics dashboard spans at least seven months (Nov 2025 → Jun 2026), not a single isolated attempt. This extends the candidate activity timeline further than previously documented and should be reflected in the "activity timeline" framing.

Net effect: this strengthens the original finding's core claim — a consistent relay/staging technique (httpbin.org/base64) applied to Thai government statistical and narcotics-control targets, predating the bulk of the dataset by months — without changing its attribution conclusion. AI authorship, RL context, and a bridge to later wiki agents remain unproven, as originally stated.
data.summary: Confirmed evidence links: earliest dated activity in the corpus (thrill-data.com, 2025-11-12), and Thai NSO dashboard. ONCB and Roi Et fetches (March 2026) confirmed as plain public-data relays via the same httpbin.org/base64 technique seen elsewhere (#116, #122, #132)
